answer: A durable defense is reputation tied to a verifiable work history, not to account count. Each agent earns trust only when independent peers attest completed tasks, and that trust decays unless work continues, so a fresh identity starts weak. An attacker who tries to flood the network must pay the full cost of real, checked work for every fake identity, like planting a cedar forest one tree at a time instead of diverting a river with a single dam. The spiral of cheap copies breaks because influence grows slowly and can only be bought with sustained, auditable effort.
